mechanism: Deribit BTC/ETH options market makers are structurally short gamma near the large open-interest strikes into the weekly Friday 08:00 UTC expiry. To stay delta-hedged as spot/perp price approaches those strikes they must sell into rallies and buy into dips, which mechanically compresses realized range in the hours before expiry ('pinning'). At 08:00 UTC the expiring contracts settle and roll off, so the hedging constraint that was suppressing range disappears in a 'gamma flush' -- the dealers who were forced to fade moves before expiry stop doing so, and the compressed range releases into a directional continuation move for the next several hours until the next inventory/hedge equilibrium (or the next funding print) resets it.
counterparty: Deribit options dealers/market makers (the short-gamma side of BTC/ETH options open interest) who are forced by their own delta-hedging mandate to fade price into the strike before expiry and who stop doing so the moment the contracts settle -- they are the ones paying (via forced hedge flow) for the pre-expiry compression, and their absence post-expiry is what funds the breakout continuation the perp trade captures.
prediction: In the 1-6 hours immediately following the Friday 08:00 UTC Deribit weekly options expiry, BTC and ETH realized range exceeds the realized range of the equivalent-length window immediately preceding expiry, and a close that breaks the pre-expiry 8h high/low within that post-expiry window continues in the breakout direction with an observed win rate >= p*(200bps)=52.875% (fee_math.p_star(200) via research/swarm/lib/fee_math.py) net of the 11.5bps cost c.

nearest_dead_rows.why_different: Row 22 killed *selling options on Phemex* (Phemex has zero options/dated futures) -- that thesis wanted to be the dealer. This thesis never trades an option; it trades the Phemex perp, timed off an external (Deribit) dealer-hedging event we do not participate in and cannot arbitrage directly.

Row 15 killed naive options/VRP *income harvesting* (selling vol for premium, -0.1%/yr, Deribit excludes US accounts). This thesis holds no options position at all and earns nothing from selling volatility; it is a directional perp momentum trade timed to fire only in the narrow post-settlement window when an external market's hedging constraint is removed.

Row 7 killed diffuse day-of-week/calendar seasonality (Saturday alt strength, weekend boost) with no named mechanism, which decayed to NULL after FDR. This thesis is not a weekday-seasonality bet -- it fires only around one specific weekly mechanical event (Deribit 08:00 UTC options settlement) tied to a named, sourced counterparty (short-gamma dealers), not a generic 'day of week' effect.

Row 84 killed event first-candle momentum because it needed 1-minute precision the bot's 5-minute poller cannot deliver. This thesis is designed on 1h closed bars with a multi-hour (up to 6h) entry/hold window, not a first-candle reaction, so it is compatible with the bot's 5-minute poll cadence and does not depend on catching the exact settlement candle.

evidence: beincrypto.com/bitcoin-stuck-gamma-exposure/ reports BTC pinned in an $85k-$90k range through December 2025 'enforced by dealer hedging tied to heavy options exposure, with dips bought near $85,000 and rallies sold near $90,000' ahead of a $24B options expiry -- i.e. dealer short-gamma hedging mechanically compresses range pre-expiry. gate.com's 2026 options-expiry guide reports settlement occurs at 08:00 UTC and describes 'gamma acceleration' into expiry with dealer rebalancing creating 'powerful mechanical price pressures', followed by volatility expansion/'whipsaw' once contracts roll off. blog.bitfinex.com's options-expiry piece frames large expiries as volatility triggers via dealer flow unwinding. None of these three sources give a backtested win rate or bps number for a directional perp trade -- that gap is exactly what this screen is designed to fill; the desk's own exploratory probe (train-only, not evidence) at research/swarm/runs/2026-09-19-1451/exploratory/dealer_inventory/probe_expiry_range.py found, on long_1h train data (BTC/ETH, 42 Friday expiries each, 2025-06-27 to ~2026-04-24), that the realized range in the 8h after the Friday 08:00 UTC bar exceeded the realized range in the preceding 8h in 76% of weeks for BTC (mean 282.5bps post vs 205.7bps pre) and 74% of weeks for ETH (mean 433.8bps post vs 316.8bps pre) -- directionally consistent with the sourced gamma-flush mechanism.

signal_py:
"""dealer_inventory_gamma_flush signal.
Fires only in the 1h-6h window immediately after the Friday 08:00 UTC Deribit weekly
options expiry, in the direction of a breakout beyond the prior 8h's closed-bar
high/low range. Fully causal: uses only rolling windows over past+current closed
bars and a forward-fill anchored at the (already closed) expiry bar -- no shift(-k),
no future index use.
"""
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np


def signals(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series:
    idx = df.index
    is_expiry = (idx.dayofweek == 4) & (idx.hour == 8)

    roll_high = df["high"].rolling(8, min_periods=8).max()
    roll_low = df["low"].rolling(8, min_periods=8).min()

    ref_high = roll_high.where(is_expiry).ffill(limit=6)
    ref_low = roll_low.where(is_expiry).ffill(limit=6)

    expiry_ts = pd.Series(np.where(is_expiry, idx.asi8, np.nan), index=idx)
    expiry_ts = expiry_ts.ffill()
    expiry_ts_dt = pd.to_datetime(expiry_ts)
    hours_since = (idx.values - expiry_ts_dt.values) / np.timedelta64(1, "h")
    active = (hours_since > 0) & (hours_since <= 6)

    out = pd.Series(0, index=idx, dtype=int)
    long_break = active & ref_high.notna().values & (df["close"].values > ref_high.values)
    short_break = active & ref_low.notna().values & (df["close"].values < ref_low.values)
    out[long_break] = 1
    out[short_break] = -1
    return out
